heard: A hundred million dollar Mars orbiter vanished from a simple math mix-up. Most people assume it was a sudden rocket failure, but the truth hid in software. Lockheed Martin built the spacecraft to calculate thrusters using pound-force seconds. Meanwhile, NASA navigation software expected metric newton seconds for those exact thrusters. Because one pound force equals about 4.45 Newtons, the system treated force as 22% of its actual value. Those tiny uncorrected errors accumulated over a nine-month journey across space. On September 23, 1999, the probe plunged to a lethal altitude of just 35 miles. Navigators spotted discrepancies earlier, but managers dismissed their warnings because proper paperwork was missing. That fatal refusal to file correct forms is why a hundred-million-dollar Mars orbiter vanished from a simple math mix-up.
